models_evaluated: Aidoc FDA-cleared intracranial aneurysm detection algorithm

links.outcome: Operational yield metrics (rEDR, gain-to-pain ratio, NNE) by care setting
links.effect: Favorable in inpatients (rEDR 78.3%, GPR 2.57, NNE 28.9) and emergency (rEDR 37.1%, GPR 1.0, NNE 85.3); unfavorable in outpatients (rEDR 14.1%, GPR 0.67, NNE 130.3).
links.quote: Operational metrics were most favorable in inpatients (rEDR 78.3%, GPR 2.57, NNE 28.9) and emergency (rEDR 37.1%, GPR 1.0, NNE 85.3) and were unfavorable in outpatients (rEDR 14.1%, GPR 0.67, NNE 130.3).

links.outcome: Prospective AI vs blinded radiologist performance in shadow mode on live CTAs
links.effect: Shadow mode on 3,856 CTAs yielded AI sensitivity 0.846 vs radiologist 0.718, similar specificity (0.987 vs 0.985), and revealed setting-specific variability in operational metrics before activation.
links.quote: Sensitivity of AI alone (0.846, 0.787-0.894) exceeded radiologist alone (0.718, 0.649-0.779), with similar specificity (radiologist: 0.985, 0.981-0.989; AI: 0.987, 0.983-0.991).

models_evaluated: Aidoc AI algorithm for brain CTA aneurysm detection

links.outcome: Setting-specific incremental detection yield and operational burden
links.effect: Outpatients: rEDR 14.1%, GPR 0.67, NNE 130.3; inpatients: rEDR 78.3%, GPR 2.57, NNE 28.9; emergency: rEDR 37.1%, GPR 1.0, NNE 85.3.
links.quote: Operational metrics were most favorable in inpatients (rEDR 78.3%, GPR 2.57, NNE 28.9) and emergency (rEDR 37.1%, GPR 1.0, NNE 85.3) and were unfavorable in outpatients (rEDR 14.1%, GPR 0.67, NNE 130.3).

links.outcome: Aneurysms detected by radiologists but missed by AI
links.effect: Radiologist-only aneurysms were mostly 3 to 5 mm (18 of 33, 54.5%); AI-alone sensitivity was 0.846, 0.787-0.894.
links.quote: Most AI-only aneurysms were <3 mm (31 of 55, 56.4%); radiologist-only were mostly 3 to 5 mm (18 of 33, 54.5%).

links.effect: Favorable in inpatients (GPR 2.57) and emergency (GPR 1.0) but unfavorable in outpatients (GPR 0.67).
links.quote: Operational metrics were most favorable in inpatients (rEDR 78.3%, GPR 2.57, NNE 28.9) and emergency (rEDR 37.1%, GPR 1.0, NNE 85.3) and were unfavorable in outpatients (rEDR 14.1%, GPR 0.67, NNE 130.3).

links.effect: Shadow-mode testing identified variable setting-specific metrics, informing clinical deployment decisions.
links.quote: The AI tool demonstrated favorable operational performance, supporting clinical deployment in real-world practice, although setting-specific metrics were variable.
